order_description: Implantation of a hypoglossal nerve neurostimulator system (stimulation lead, pulse generator and respiratory sensor) for obstructive sleep apnea

candidates.title: Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: Candidates L38398, L38528 and L38307 are the same HGNS policy issued by different contractors, so any one applies. The record fits the typical criteria: severe OSA (AHI 32) confirmed by polysomnography, documented CPAP intolerance despite mask and pressure changes, BMI 29.5 (under 32), central/mixed apneas about 8% of AHI, and a drug-induced sleep endoscopy done before implant. Contraindications were screened. Selected L38398 as the first matching candidate.

criteria.policy_text: Beneficiary is 22 years of age or older
criteria.explanation: The patient is a 42-year-old male, which satisfies the age requirement of 22 or older.

criteria.policy_text: Body mass index (BMI) is less than 35 kg/m2
criteria.explanation: BMI was 29.5 kg/m2 on 2029-04-26, below 35. The 2018 problem-list entry for BMI 30+ (R11) is historical and superseded by the current measurement.

criteria.policy_text: A polysomnography (PSG) is performed within 24 months of first consultation for HGNS implant
criteria.explanation: The only documented PSG was attended polysomnography on 2026-10-02 (R45), which diagnosed OSA (R28). The first HGNS consultation was with sleep medicine on 2029-03-31 (R36). That interval is about 29.9 months, which exceeds 24 months. No other PSG within 24 months of the first consultation is documented.

criteria.policy_text: Predominantly obstructive events (central and mixed apneas less than 25% of the total AHI)
criteria.explanation: Central and mixed apneas are 8% of the total AHI, below the 25% threshold.

criteria.policy_text: AHI is 15 to 65 events per hour
criteria.explanation: The diagnostic polysomnography on 2026-10-02 recorded an AHI of 32 events per hour, within 15 to 65.

criteria.policy_text: Documentation that demonstrates CPAP failure (AHI greater than 15 despite CPAP usage) or CPAP intolerance (less than 4 hours per night, 5 nights per week or the CPAP has been returned) including shared decision making that the patient was intolerant of CPAP despite consultation with a sleep expert
criteria.explanation: The alternative of CPAP intolerance applies. Average use was 1.5 hours on nights used, and CPAP was used on 6 of the last 30 nights, both below the intolerance threshold. The residual AHI of 8 on CPAP does not show failure, but intolerance alone satisfies the criterion. Shared decision making is documented in a conversation between the patient and the sleep medicine physician (R45), who is the sleep expert, and the otolaryngologist also documented it with the patient (R46). Both are provider-patient conversations, as the SDM definition in Limitations.5 requires.

criteria.policy_text: Absence of complete concentric collapse at the soft palate level as seen on a drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) procedure
criteria.explanation: The DISE report of 2029-05-22 documents partial anteroposterior collapse at the soft palate and no complete concentric collapse.

criteria.policy_text: No other anatomical findings that would compromise performance of device (e.g., tonsil size 3 or 4 per standardized tonsillar hypertrophy grading scale)
criteria.explanation: Tonsils are size 1 on the Brodsky scale, the neck is supple with no masses, and Mallampati class is II. The DISE shows partial lateral wall and tongue base collapse and no epiglottic collapse, but no record entry identifies these or any other finding as compromising device performance.

criteria.criterion: Limitations.3 (contraindications other than active serious mental illness)
criteria.policy_text: Hypoglossal nerve neurostimulation is considered not medically reasonable and necessary when any of the following contraindications are present (central and mixed apneas more than one-quarter of AHI; implantable device interaction; BMI 35 or greater; neuromuscular disease; hypoglossal-nerve palsy; severe pulmonary disease; moderate-to-severe pulmonary arterial hypertension; severe valvular heart disease; NYHA III or IV heart failure; recent MI or severe arrhythmia within 6 months; persistent uncontrolled hypertension; nonrespiratory sleep disorders; pregnancy; MRI requirement; inability to operate the sleep remote; compromised neurological control of the upper airway)
criteria.explanation: None of these contraindications is documented as present. The physician's screen (R46) records no neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal palsy, severe pulmonary disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, valvular disease or heart failure, no MI or severe arrhythmia in 6 months, controlled blood pressure, no other sleep disorder, no implanted devices, no anticipated MRI, ability to operate the remote, and no condition affecting upper airway neurological control. Central and mixed apneas are 8% (R45) and BMI is 29.5 (R41). The pregnancy item does not apply to this male patient.

criteria.criterion: Limitations.3 (active serious mental illness that reduces ADLs and interferes with operating the device)
criteria.policy_text: An active, serious mental illness that reduces the ability to carry out ADLs and would interfere with the patient's ability to operate the HNS and report problems to the attending provider
criteria.explanation: The otolaryngologist documents no serious mental illness (R46). However, dependent drug abuse is listed as active (R2), and there are repeated overdose entries (R17, R18, R21, R27). Social isolation and stress are also active (R23, R24). The record does not assess whether any of these reduces ADL performance or the ability to operate the device and report problems, so this cannot be determined.

criteria.policy_text: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation for the treatment of OSA must be furnished in accordance with the accepted standards of medical practice in a setting appropriate to the patient's medical needs and condition.
criteria.explanation: The record lists an operating room environment (R30) without a date or link to the planned implant. It does not document the setting in which the implantation will be performed.

decision_explanation: Covered Indications.3 is not met. The only documented PSG (2026-10-02) was about 29.9 months before the first HGNS consultation on 2029-03-31, which exceeds the 24-month requirement, and no other PSG is documented. Because a required criterion is not met, the order is denied. The serious mental illness contraindication and the implant setting also remain undetermined from the record.
